chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Honor the bread, for it has been worked upon by much of the creation between the Throne and the earth and what is in it.'

Then he said to those around him: 'Shall I inform you?' They said, 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah, may the fathers and mothers be sacrificed for you.' So he said: 'There was a Prophet among those who were before you, called Daniel, and he gave a loaf of bread to the owner of a crossing so that he might cross with it.'
So the owner of the crossing threw down the bread and said: 'What do I do with this bread? The bread is with us, it is trampled by feet.'
So when Daniel saw that from him, he raised his hand to the sky and said: 'O Allah, honor the bread, for You have seen, O Lord, what this servant did and what he said.'
So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to the sky to withhold the rain, and revealed to the earth to become layers like pottery.
So they did not rain until their affairs reached such that some of them ate each other.

So when what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, intended from that reached them, a woman said to another, and for both of them were two children: 'O So-and-so, come, let I and you eat my child today, and when it is tomorrow, we will eat your child.'
She said to her, 'Yes.' So they ate him.
So when they became hungry afterwards, the other enticed her to eat her child, but she refused her.
So she said to her: 'Between me and you is the Prophet of Allah.' So they brought their dispute to Daniel (peace be upon him).
So he said to them both, 'And has the matter reached to what I see?' They said to him, 'Yes, O Prophet of Allah, and even more difficult.'

So he raised his hand to the sky and said: 'O Allah, return upon us with Your Grace, and the Grace of Your Mercy, and do not punish the children and those in it who are good, by the sin of the owner of the crossing and his trampling of Your Bounty.'

So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded the sky: 'Rain upon the earth,' and commanded the earth: 'Grow for My creation what they have missed of your goodness, for I have shown mercy to them through the young child.'
ai.seo_question: What is the story of Prophet Daniel and the trampled bread in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* underscores the theological weight of bread by linking its physical creation to the cosmic realm, a concept rooted in Shia exegetical tradition regarding the sanctity of sustenance. The narrative of Prophet Daniel (Daniyal) illustrates how disrespect toward this divine blessing triggers a proportional cosmic response, culminating in a famine severe enough for cannibalism, yet resolved through divine mercy that spares the innocent children from the specific sin of the ferryman.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Sadaqa,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Honour the bread, for it has been worked upon by what is between the Throne and the earth and what is from the numerous of its people’.

Then he<sup>saww</sup> said to the ones around him<sup>saww</sup>: ‘Shall I<sup>saww</sup> inform you all?’ They said, ‘Yes, O Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, may the fathers and the mothers be sacrificed for you<sup>saww</sup>’. So he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘There was a Prophet<sup>as</sup> among the ones who were before you all, called Dainel<sup>as</sup>, and he<sup>asws</sup> gave the owner of the crossing a bread in order to cross with it.
So the owner of the crossing threw down the bread and said, ‘What do I do with this bread. The bread is with us’, and he trampled it with the leg.

So when Daniel<sup>as</sup> saw that from him, he<sup>as</sup> raised his<sup>as</sup> hands towards the sky, then said: ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Honour the bread, for You<sup>azwj</sup> have Seen, O Lord<sup>azwj</sup> what this servant has done and what he said’.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto the sky that it withholds the rain, and Revealed unto the earth that it become layers like the pottery.
So it did not rain to the extent that their affairs reached such that some of them ate each other.

So when (the situation) reached what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Intended from that, a woman said to another, and for both of them were parents, ‘O so and so, come, let I and you both, eat my parents today, and when it is tomorrow, we both eat your parents’.

So when she came over afterwards the other enticing to eat her parents, she prevented her, and she said, ‘Between me and you is a Prophet<sup>as</sup> of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. So they both brought their dispute to Daniel<sup>as</sup>.

So he<sup>as</sup> said to them both: ‘And has the matter reached to what I<sup>as</sup> see?’ She said to him<sup>as</sup>, ‘Yes, O Prophet<sup>as</sup> of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and even more difficult’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So he<sup>as</sup> raised his<sup>as</sup> hands towards the sky, so he<sup>as</sup> said; ‘O Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Return upon us with Your<sup>azwj</sup> Grace, and Grace of Your<sup>azwj</sup> Mercy, and do not Punish the children, and the good ones in it, by the sin of the owner of the crossing, and his disrespecting Your<sup>azwj</sup> Bounty’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Commanded the sky that: “Rain for Me<sup>azwj</sup> upon the earth”, and Commanded the earth that “Grow for My<sup>azwj</sup> Creatures, so Give them from your goodness, for I<sup>azwj</sup> am being Merciful to them due to the young children’.
en.sarwar: 2. Afi ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas’adah ibn Sadaqah who has said the following: “It is a narration of abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, from the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause.
He (the Messenger of Allah) once said, ‘You must treat bread with reverence because from the throne to earth and what is in it, a large number of His creatures have worked for it (to make it ready).’

He (the Messenger of Allah) then said, ‘Will you like if I tell you something?’ They replied, ‘Yes, O Messenger of Allah, we pray to Allah to keep the fathers and mothers in service for your cause.’ He (the Messenger of Allah) said, ‘Among the Prophets before you there was a Prophet called Daniel. He once gave one loaf of bread to the owner of the crossing (means) to help for crossing.
He threw the bread away saying, ‘It is of no use for me. We crush bread under our foot.’
When Daniel saw it, he raised his hands to the sky and said, ‘O Lord, make bread revered because I saw what this servant just did to it and what he said.’
Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, sent revelation to the sky and told it to withhold rain and the earth to turn into a piece of pottery.’
It did not rain and they ended up eating each other.
When their condition reached the point which Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, wanted, one woman said to the other, who each had a child, to one day eat the child of one of them.
The other woman agreed and they ate the child.
When they became hungry again the other woman demanded to eat the child of the other woman but she refused saying, ‘Between us there is the Prophet of Allah.’
They went to Daniel, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, for judgment.
He said to them, ‘I can see to what degree the condition has reached.’ They said, ‘Yes, O Prophet of Allah and it is more difficult.’

He raised his hands to the sky and said, ‘O Lord, return to us with Your generosity, and the extra of Your mercy and do not make the children to suffer because of the sins of the owner of the crossing and his disrespecting Your bounties.’

Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, commanded the sky to send rain and earth to grow produce for His creatures what they had lost of the goodness because He had turned to them with kindness through the small child.’”
